article.summary: A local-first TypeScript memory layer for coding agents using Markdown files, with an optional qmd search helper and CLI/MCP interfaces. This is a source review, not a measured evaluation.

who_what.text: The official README describes AgentMemory as a local-first, MIT-licensed memory layer for coding agents. The public GitHub repository is owned by jayzeng; this review did not confirm a wider maintainer group.

architecture.text: Code observation: the default user-local directory contains MEMORY.md, SCRATCHPAD.md, dated daily files, and topic files. AGENT_MEMORY_DIR can redirect the store. Markdown is the documented source of truth; qmd search is optional.

The README documents a CLI and an MCP server over newline-delimited JSON-RPC stdio. The MCP server exposes five tools and delegates to the same core logic as corresponding CLI commands, rather than providing a separate memory implementation.

behavior.text: Write: core writes append timestamped daily and topic entries and append or overwrite MEMORY.md. Entries can include a shortened session identifier and source URI. Credential-pattern redaction is applied before storing entry content.

Update and deletion: long-term memory supports overwrite; the scratchpad supports marking items done/undoing and clearing completed items. The inspected MCP tools and core write surface did not expose per-entry deletion. The README describes direct file edits/deletion, and the CLI can remove the full memory directory when explicitly asked to uninstall with data.

Retrieval: documented operations read a target, build context, and search. Keyword mode is available; qmd is optional for local search. This inspection does not establish ranking quality, recall, or abstention.

Scope: memory is stored in a user-local directory, with AGENT_MEMORY_DIR as a path override. The inspected surfaces do not establish tenant authentication, project authorization, or enforced cross-user isolation.

Provenance: entries can retain a timestamp, shortened session identifier, and optional source URI. These fields support traceability but do not establish structured claim-level evidence, source trust, or entailment.

Source-visible efficiency and observability: plain Markdown is inspectable without a database service; qmd indexing/search is optional; writes schedule qmd updates; and the MCP transport reuses core logic. No runtime performance or operational metric was measured.

metrics.evidence: Read/context/search interfaces are documented and implemented; answerable recall and calibrated abstention were not measured.
Overwrite and append operations are source-visible; no correction or stale-value workload was run.
Manual file deletion and whole-directory removal are documented, but no deletion completeness or leakage workload was run.
A configurable local storage path is visible in code; no cross-user or cross-project isolation probes were run.
Optional source URIs can be stored; no claim-support precision or citation-coverage workload was run.
No retrieval latency measurements were collected.
Writes schedule qmd update work, but no delay from write to successful retrieval was measured.
No token or cost measurements were collected.
The source of truth is Markdown with optional qmd indexing, but no storage-efficiency measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded code/documentation review at the verified main head. The system, tests, and benchmarks were not run; implementation structure does not establish runtime behavior or quality.
The inspected sources do not establish exact qmd failure recovery, concurrent writer safety, cleanup of separately configured derived indexes, retrieval quality, or security-redaction coverage.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. Source observations are not measurements; the project metric definition, fixture, and status record are protocol references only.
